text: The Supreme Court of Chile is the highest judicial body in the country and oversees the administration of lower courts, located in the capital city of Santiago. Unlike some judicial systems, it does not possess judicial review powers—meaning it cannot establish binding precedent or strike down laws—and instead decides cases on a case-by-case basis. Trials are conducted in salas, which are chambers composed of at least five judges, with the most senior judge presiding. Supreme Court members are appointed by the President from a list of five nominees provided by the current justices, requiring that two of the nominees be senior judges from appellate courts and the other three may have no prior judicial experience. The President’s selection must be approved by a two-thirds majority in the Senate. Justices must be at least 36 years old and serve until the mandatory retirement age of 75, unless they are removed for "notorious abandonment of duty" as determined by a majority of both chambers of Congress. The Court consists of twenty-one members, known as ministers (ministros), one of whom serves a two-year term as President of the Supreme Court. Due to the retirement age of 75, the Court's composition changes frequently. The Chilean Supreme Court has participated in significant human rights cases involving former dictator Augusto Pinochet and has issued controversial rulings on gay rights. On September 21, 2007, the court accepted Peru’s request to extradite former Peruvian president Alberto Fujimori on human rights and corruption charges. The Court’s location is at 33°26′21″S 70°39′11″W (33.43917°S 70.65306°W). Note: List last updated on 21 August 2023.[1]
